subject: Yoto's $128M year came off a $100 box, but the profit is in $6-$15 cards
takeaway: Sell the thing they buy once at cost, and own the thing they buy again. The model only prints money when the repeat purchase is technically or legally impossible to buy from anyone else.
recency: Founded 2017 (Music Business Worldwide, 2024); in 2026 it became the poster child of the kids-tech backlash, profiled by The New York Times in late June/early July 2026 and by Forbes on 18 August 2026, weeks after a Los Angeles jury found Meta and Google liable on 25 March 2026 for designing feeds to addict a minor.
confidence: Medium-high: 2024 revenue and losses come from Yoto's filed accounts as reported by the Financial Times and relayed in a July 2026 teardown; pricing is public. Card-level gross margin is not disclosed, and a GetLatka estimate of $44.2M ARR contradicts the filings, so treat third-party revenue estimates as noise.

subject: A 30-person company that owns zero GPUs manages over $100M of them
takeaway: When a market only sells in one size or one term, the distance between how a thing is sold and how it is actually needed is itself a business. You do not need to own the asset to get paid for closing that distance, but you do need to be willing to hold the risk nobody else will.
recency: Founded 2023; closed a $40M Series A at a $300M valuation in December 2025 (DCD, citing WSJ), hired Voltage Park's ex-CEO as CTO, and spent 2026 getting written up as the stock market for GPUs (DailyDropout.FYI, July 2026).
confidence: Medium-high: funding terms, headcount, and the >$100M-of-hardware-managed figure all come from a December 2025 DCD report citing the WSJ. Revenue and take rate are not public, so the spread economics are inferred from the model, not verified.

subject: Crosby's 1,000th contract took 173 days. Now it does 1,000 every three weeks.
takeaway: If you bill by the hour, getting better at your job lowers your income. Fix the price to a tightly defined outcome and every efficiency you find becomes margin instead of a smaller invoice, which is the only way a service business gets software-like economics.
recency: Came out of stealth June 17, 2025 as an AI-native law firm; raised a $20M Series A in October 2025 and a $60M Series B led by Lux and Index on March 31, 2026.
confidence: Medium-high: funding terms, contract throughput, turnaround rate and the fixed-fee model are all stated by the founders on Crosby's own 2025-2026 posts and pricing copy. Exact per-document price and ARR are not public, so the revenue figure is an explicit estimate.
